utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are ready to proceed with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Before we proceed with cross-examination, I would like to inform this Trial Chamber that the Defence is in possession of one binder of documents. Well, the basic reason why we have this break, that was the process of reviewing of the documents by the Prosecution, as we all remember in last Friday, I believe. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So briefly, just for the record, at the end of the -- yesterday's working hours, 4.30, I believe, something like that, we got one binder of these documents pursuant to Rule 68 from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yeah, you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, just wait. Let him finish, and then you'll be able to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe Your Honour, in order to clarify that, maybe my learned friend would like to give a precise thing. Maybe we could hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You inform the Court what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I don't know why this reaction was. Anyhow, so the Defence for Mr. Blagoje Simic was not able at all to inform our client what the contents of these documents are due to the well-known limitations with regard to the visit at the UNDU. So I kindly ask on that basis to have a certain period of time to consult with my client because I do believe that certain portion of these documents might have relevance in the course of the cross-examination of my client. Of course, a certain portion of these documents got certain -- impact also on the examination-in-chief. And in general to some extent of the Defence strategy. But we are not in a situation to discuss that any more because this part of the examination-in-chief actually was concluded, so we cannot go into past. Another thing: A certain number of documents are not translated, so that's -- that's another problem which I'm facing now. I have -- virtually I have to, I would say, to explain to my client what is in certain documents. He practically is not able by himself to go through these papers and then to be familiar, and then the Defence could have a certain level of -- a certain level of quality, in terms of the relation between attorney and his client. Otherwise, I have to go through all these documents and to explain to him and to translate to him in person. So what I would like to kindly suggest to this Trial Chamber: Let's see if approximately one hour would be enough for us to consult with regard to these documents. In the meantime, if our learned friend could provide us with the -- we shall inform them about the relevant documents we would like -- that we would like to have in -- we have to have in English. And then in the meantime, if they can check that with the -- with their records and interpreters unit, if we would be in possession of this translation, then that would certainly speed up things. So basically there is no, I would say, big or extreme problems with that issue, unless the Trial Chamber wishes to give some other guidelines with regard to these procedures. I believe that we could proceed today with the cross-examination by all means. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I have no objection to him taking an hour or so to meet with his client and go over those documents. I have no objection to that. However, what I'd like to do is address this whole issue and what has happened in the last week and just explain to the Court the whole situation that's occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Last week we came across seven files on Dr. Blagoje Simic, and they were -- and we came across them just a day or so prior to cross-examination. We were probably a little bit tired. We were just starting the Defence case and we were gearing up for it. We panicked and we panicked for no reason. We were under the impression that there was a major problem that existed. We were alarmed, we were concerned, and we notified the Chamber immediately. In our panic, we were wrong. It was a false alarm. There is no disclosure problem. There is no problem with the discovery process. There are no Rule 68 violations. The discovery process has been ongoing for years. We are confident that there is no Rule 68 problem. Rather, our Rule 68 obligation has been met and it is continuing to be met. I sincerely apologise for this alleged crisis and wasting the Court's time. However, what it turned out to be was no wasting of time. We were able to review, do a full review -- was conducted by our senior Prosecutor on the case, Gramsci Di Fazio, and worked over the weekends and during the days and during the evenings and we found the following: Our initial impression that no major searches were done was wrong. In 1998 an all-system search was performed on defendants, witnesses, words, and places. In 1999, an all-system search was performed on defendants and witnesses. In the year 2000, an all-systems search was performed on defendants and witnesses. In the year 2001, prior to trial, an all-systems search was performed on defendants and witnesses. This week we are lucky to have Nancy Paterson, who was the original Prosecutor on this case, who took this case from the investigation through the indictment, and who left the office or retired from this office just prior to the trial. She's here on corporate business, non-related to the ICTY, and she visited our office. We were able to sit down and discuss the matter with her. She told us about her 1998 search. She explained that she's an American prosecutor, that Rule 68 emanates from the United States, that she is well aware of the Rule 68 Rules, having been a prosecutor for many years, and she is obsessive about discovery. She ordered these annual searches to be performed. She noted that the all-systems search was performed in 1998, in 1999 an all-systems search of witnesses and defendants was performed again. Also in 1999 she split up the witnesses among three attorneys and each one of them did internal-source searches to see if they could come up with anything. She also ran these all-systems searches of witnesses and defendants in the year 2000. And in the year 2001, it appears that she ran two all-systems searches, one in the January/February period, and the second just before she left, so in -- and the results came out in June and July, just prior to trial. The first one -- it's not clear. It's her memory. The second one, we're certain of, the June/July one, because we have the documents and we have the dates on the -- in the relation to the all-systems search. In February of 2001 she appeared at some motions and she discussed disclosure and she was explaining how she had complied with disclosure. After Nancy Paterson leaves, Aisling Reidy takes over that chore. She continues the witness searches on her own. She does the internal witness searches and she occasionally finds documents. And this Court recalls how at different periods we would find documents and hand them over. In fact, there was an exculpatory document relating to Esad Dagovic. We handed it over as soon as we found it, and this Court was -- ordered him back for cross-examination, which he did in fact come back and he was confronted with that document. In 2001, just around the start of trial, the ICTY obtained a collection of military documents, a quarter of a million documents on disks. As this Court recalls, Aisling Reidy got together with the computer section and they ran a search of those. We also made those disks or the computer system or whatever available to Defence to search. We have now just completed additional searches. With regard to Blagoje Simic, we've completed a search of those seven volumes. We have found no exculpatory evidence, no Rule 68 evidence. I just received a message from Gramsci Di Fazio that he has completed his review of the Tadic and Zaric documents, and there are six documents he's interested in and would like to discuss among the three counsel here to see if they are -- if they're Rule 68 or if they're material. Under reciprocal discovery they have to be turned over. But until I actually see the documents and the three of us sit down, I can't comment on those. But we're talking about just six documents. An all-systems search has never been required by this Court, by any Court here, by Rule 68, or by an order. It's not necessary and in many situations it's a waste of time. What we do it as is a last-minute insurance policy to make sure everything is right. We have been doing that. We are continuing to do that. We have just done it on all the defendants. We've done it on the witnesses this year. We -- so we have resolved the matter. Going in and looking at that history, we know that no problem exists. There are no minor problems that exist. A commendable job has been done and we apologise to the Court for the false alarm. But as I said, it has enabled us to go out and see what in fact we have done. Now, with regard to Blagoje Simic, he has not invoked reciprocal discovery. He is not entitled to reciprocal discovery. We found no Rule 68 or exculpatory materials relating to Dr. Blagoje Simic. We have found several documents, most of them are orders that he signed, whether he was on the War Presidency, the Crisis Staff, or the Serbian Assembly of Bosanski Samac. In the rush to get these over to them, I can say that we haven't already provided these documents to him, because we haven't been able to check. We had to work around the clock to get this stuff over to him. So what we've done is given him a binder. Some statements, but mostly documents that he has signed. If his name was on it, signing it, we gave over to him. He is not entitled to that. They are not Rule 68. Most of the information is inculpatory. However, as a courtesy, as we have done from the beginning of this trial and prior to the trial starting, anything that's material, we hand over to him even though he has not invoked reciprocal discovery. So the package we gave him yesterday, he is not entitled to and we are providing that as a courtesy. I have no objection and the Prosecution has no objection to him sitting down with his client and going over those. We have no problem at with that at all. If we would like an hour or so, it's not a problem to us. However, the key thing I want to tell you today is there was no 68 material relating to Blagoje Simic. I will check with co-counsel on those six other documents. And finally, we have checked. We have done a commendable job in discovery and disclosure. There is no Rule 68 problem relating to the Prosecution of this case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Your Honour. With regard to the Tadic material, we did not receive those by the close of business yesterday. We received those between 6.00 and 7.00 last night, so that's why we didn't have the chance to report to you first thing this morning on those. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is of the view that since Rule 68 is an ongoing obligation and that not only now, or maybe even in the future before the trial comes to an end, documents may still come to the attention of the Prosecution. The Trial Chamber is of the view that we shall proceed with the case. Cross-examination will continue. However, the accused will be given an opportunity during the re-examination stage, should anything come up, to go beyond the cross-examination in re-examination to cover what else may come up in case of the documents that have just been handed over. So the cross-examination will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Miroslav Tadic has certain questions for Mr. Simic. I don't think we will take more than 15 minutes. As far as I know, the Zaric Defence also has a few questions as well. These are questions that are simply related to my client. So before the cross-examination, I would like put these questions that have to do with my client and his role and place in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: BLAGOJE SIMIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no need for know introduce myself to you. My first question will be: For how long have you known Mr. Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since the war period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "the war period," I assume that you are talking about the 17th of April, 1992. Is that what you mean by "the war period" or do you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the examination conducted by my colleague, I got the impression that you took active part in political life from 1990. That's what you said, that you then acceded to the Serb Democratic Party. Now, my question is the following: Do you know that Miroslav Tadic in that period and subsequently -- do you know whether he was a member of any political party in the territory of Bosanski Samac and beyond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of his being a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him at any party meeting or political meeting before the conflict broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to witness to be shown document D59/3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While the usher is bringing the document, I'm going to remind you that during the examination-in-chief you said to my colleague, Mr. Pantelic, that the Crisis Staff was established around the 19th of April and that my client became a member of the Crisis Staff somewhat later. You said specifically around the 20th of April. I don't know if you had the opportunity of reading the interview of my client which is an exhibit introduced by the prosecutor. This is the interview that he gave to the Prosecution. He claims that he became a member of the Crisis Staff when he was appointed the commander of the civilian protection staff. In this document -- first of all, are you aware of this document? Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date on this document is the 23rd of April, 1992. Is that the day when Miroslav Tadic, since he was appointed president of the Crisis Staff of civilian protection staff, is that the day when he was appointed a member of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 3 of this decision and could you please comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The civilian protection is within the realm of the Defence Ministry, and the final decision had to be passed by the Defence Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the preamble to this decision, the introductory part, I mean. In your opinion, is that the reason why Miroslav Tadic became a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also in response to my colleague's question, you said that the composition of the Crisis Staff and of the War Presidency was not identical. You said that the members of the Crisis Staff were those persons whose names were on the payroll for May. As for the membership of the War Presidency, you linked that to the decree of Republika Srpska, which prescribed who would be a member of the War Presidency. My question is very specific: Was Miroslav Tadic a member of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic ever take part in decision-making in the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Miroslav Tadic from time to time as a member of the exchange commission and as a member and president of the civilian protection staff, that he came to the Presidency from time to time and submitted certain reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Like Velimir Martic [As interpreted], who was president of the exchange commission, I assume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to correct the name here. It is Maslic, M-a-s-l-i-c, not Martic, the way it says here. Now, did Miroslav Tadic have any position in the system of government when the municipal assembly started functioning again in the month of January 1993, apart from being a member of the exchange commission and being on the civilian protection staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Miroslav Tadic before the war, during the war, and after the war -- do you know whether he was ever, in those periods, an assemblyman in any assembly, a member of any assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I have clarification on the answer no. Is it no, you don't know? Is it no, he was not a member of any of the assemblies?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in one more topic that you referred to my colleague, and that is your knowledge in respect of how Stevan Todorovic, as you said, mistreated members of the Crisis Staff including Miroslav Tadic. Do you remember that Miroslav Tadic proposed to you that you distance yourselves and that you make every effort for Stevan Todorovic to be replaced? If you know about that, could you please describe this. And if you don't know about it, I'm not going to ask you any further questions with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that a few times Miroslav Tadic insisted that a way be found for Todorovic to be replaced. But I do not remember the exact date or the exact occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My final question has to do with the final question of my colleague Mr. Pantelic, who presented to you allegations from the indictment. My question is whether ever during the war or after the war you talked to Mr. Tadic or made proposals to him or did you receive his proposals to move the non-Serb population outside of the municipality of Samac, out of their homes against their will.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was for the period before the war as well. So does this answer of yours pertain to the pre-war period as well, since you said that you did not know him before the war and could not talk to him -- I assume --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please stop speaking at the same time as the witness. The interpreter cannot follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: ...the moving of the non-Serb population from their homes in the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to put a few questions to you in relation to your general relationship with Mr. Zaric, and the first question is the following: Is it correct that you and Mr. Simo Zaric lived in the same apartment building in a street which was then called the street of Edvard Kardelj. In Bosanski Samac the building was known as number 62.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the end of 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So in 1991, late 1991, you moved into the building known as the building number 62 in Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You did not live in the same section or entrance of that apartment building, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: My colleague says that the transcript is not quite clear, so let me repeat. You did not live in the same entrance of that apartment building, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you did not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any friendly relationship with Mr. Zaric ever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was there any kind of business relationship between you and Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever present in Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simo Zaric ever go to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, was Mr. Zaric ever a member of the Serb Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that up until the 17th of April, 1992 Simo Zaric was never a member or assemblyman or deputy in the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Simo Zaric was not an assemblyman in the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac in the time period from 1990 up until the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that Mr. Zaric was not an assemblyman in the Assembly of the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not an assemblyman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Simo Zaric was not present at the meeting held on the 15th of April, 1992 which was held in the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac and where representatives of Gradacac, Orasje municipalities were present, and Odzak municipality as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that you and Mr. Zaric did not have any kind of agreements, talks, or any other contacts in the time period up until the 17th of April, 1992 and afterwards regarding the events which took place in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Could you please be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. Simo Zaric ever talk, plan, organise, make arrangements for any actions to be taken in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm that Mr. Simo Zaric was not a member of the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff of Samac Municipality ever issue any kind of orders to Simo Zaric personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Simo Zaric never submitted any reports on his actions to the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He never submitted any kind of reports to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric did not submit any reports on his work to the War Presidency either after it was established, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Ministry of Defence of the municipality of Bosanski Samac deployed Mr. Simo Zaric as a military conscript to occupy the post in the military council and to be in charge of security issues in that body? I mean in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the Ministry of Defence sent him to Odzak to implement some military affairs there, that he was sent to Odzak. But what exactly he did there, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Simo Zaric as a conscript was under the direct command of security organs of the military administration that had been introduced in Odzak municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the territory of the military administration, everybody is under the command of that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm the fact that neither the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency, nor you personally, ever asked Mr. Simo Zaric to submit any kind of reports on the way he executed his military tasks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Neither the Crisis Staff nor I personally ever asked Mr. Simo Zaric to submit any kind of reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question: You here spoke on how Mr. Stevan Todorovic terrorised some people. You also spoke about the volunteers from Serbia and certain members of the Crisis Staff. Do you know that these same people - meaning Stevan Todorovic and the individuals that had come from Serbia - persecuted Simo Zaric fiercely, sent death threats to him, and basically made his life unpleasant in a number of ways? Do you have any knowledge of this? And if so, please tell us what you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Stevan Todorovic had an especially hostile attitude with respect to Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will conclude my examination here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...what is that in the transcript. Page 17, line 10. So I kindly ask my colleague to clarify this question. It was not -- his original question was not on a proper basis translated, and the transcript does not reflect his question. It is very dubious form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean the translation is not -- or the question that counsel put to the accused is not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Your Honour. Let me just confer with my colleague to explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Let him repeat the question. That's all. The counsel knows what he's asking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can help. It is only one part of the translation of the question. The question was relatively clear -- completely clear, but the translation said here on page 17 -- just one second. It says: "You also spoke about the volunteers from Serbia and certain members of the Crisis Staff." Both these words were mentioned in Mr. Pisarevic's question, but there was -- he was referring to the statement of Mr. Blagoje Simic here about how volunteers tortured some members of the Crisis Staff, and that was the issue here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe to clear the point, can Mr. Pisarevic just repeat the question and then we'll get the answer from the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, in your testimony you spoke about certain acts of terrorising of certain members of the Crisis Staff by the chief of the Public Security Station, Mr. Stevan Todorovic, and some volunteers from Serbia. My question was: Do you know that the chief of the Public Security Station, Stevan Todorovic, and some members of the volunteer units from Serbia fiercely terrorised, persecuted, sent threats to Mr. Simo Zaric as well? Do you know anything about that? And if so, please tell the Chamber about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Stevan Todorovic had a very clear hostile attitude with respect to Simo Zaric due to his Communist pedigree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just one question before we start with the cross-examination, Your Honour. Could we have an estimated time for the cross-examination, because in that case we could plan our time for re-examination and then we can have certain plans with the witnesses -- Defence witnesses who are here at The Hague. So in terms of this coordination with the Victim's Unit, it will be useful for us to know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time -- I haven't started yet, but I'll assume I'm going to finish before the day is over. I will definitely finish before the day is over. In addition to that, when we delivered the courtesy package to Mr. -- to the assistant, Srdjan -- I'm not sure of his last name, to the assistant of Mr. Pantelic, we were told that we would receive our discovery on upcoming witnesses when we delivered our package yesterday. When I delivered the package yesterday, I was told that Igor Pantelic would deliver the information to me probably tomorrow. They're planning to put a witness on tomorrow. We have not -- still not received a summary of what this witness is going to say. We have not received any proofing notes. It would be nice that -- if sometime before this witness takes the stand we receive the discovery that we're entitled to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, number one: I didn't intervene before during the explanation of my colleague. It is the obligation on the Prosecution side to disclose any material with regard to the defendant. At latest -- I'm just speaking in general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very, very briefly. Just answer what Mr. Weiner said about the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, Your Honour -- I want to clear up the record. I'm speaking about the obligation from the Prosecution -- it is a general fact that they have to disclose that. We are not in reciprocal disclosure, but it is not a situation that we are not entitled for any material. So that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think the explanation of the Prosecution is on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's the witness -- the next witness after the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another thing: We gave the summary -- I speak personally with the -- with my colleagues about the range of testimony that our first witness will come here in capacity of former member of executive board about the events in Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anyway, as far as you're concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is no proofing notes, Your Honour. That's the basic point. And there are no -- any obligation with regard to the Defence to give any kind of -- because there is no -- there is no proofing notes. I can -- orally can inform him about the topic, about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anyway, the summaries were given because the summaries were --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The summaries were given and he will discuss all materials with regard to the executive board and Crisis Staff; which is evidence that we have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, just start cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say they've given us three or four sentences. They indicated yesterday -- for the first time they told us who the witness is, Mirko Lukic and then they said the witness will be on for a full day. Three or four sentences --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought the summaries were the same that were given to the -- that were filed also with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's three or four sentences. They're talking about putting a witness on direct examination for a day and we have three or four sentences. And no proofing notes? You want to talk about ambush, that's nothing more than ambush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So first witness will be -- according to you, Mr. Weiner, is Mirko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's what I was told yesterday. If they'd confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They are not following the list as filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And as we mentioned in our brief -- and then Mr. Mirko Lukic, who was at that time a member of executor -- will go through all these documents and exhibits. So nothing is so exceptional. We have our line of defence. And I don't see any particular reason why to expand this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, cross-examination of the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Phillip Weiner, I'm a Prosecutor at the Office of the Prosecutor here at the ICTY, and I'm going to ask you some questions over the next few hours. Having heard the evidence to date, sir, do you accept that Izet Izetbegovic and others had their teeth pulled while being held in detention in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what we just heard as translation do not correspond at all with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S -- the question that we heard in B/C/S is whether Izetbegovic and others had power in Samac. This is what we heard in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can ask the question slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept, after having heard the evidence so far, that Izet Izetbegovic and other prisoners had their teeth pulled while they were being held in detention in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many questions there. Can you put this question to me again but clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that Izet Izetbegovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We are now in the legal terms. Maybe the proper question will be: Do you know, personally know. But if he is accepting, whether he has accepting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or, you know, a fact

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you haven't been given permission to say anything. And will you sit down. There is no reason to interfere with the question by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my official objection, Your Honour. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing wrong with the question. The Prosecutor will go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, after hearing the evidence, do you accept that Izet Izetbegovic and other prisoners had their teeth pulled or forcibly removed while they were being held in detention in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that and I do not accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that non-Serb prisoners were murdered at detention facilities, at the police station, the Territorial Defence building, in Crkvina, and other locations in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It is -- it is too general a question. We don't know where, which murder was committed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. If the question is not proper, the Trial Chamber will say so. Mr. Pantelic I order outside -- out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the duty of Defence counsel is to protect the rights of my client. And therefore I think that this question is too general. There is no particular event. There is no particular name. There is no particular so-called murder. Maybe the line of questioning should be divided into these sections. That's all that I'm asking. Otherwise, it's unbelievable. How can he know in all -- in all municipality or in all area what was done? That's my duty, Your Honour, to react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The accused was listening to the evidence throughout the proceedings. And what -- and these questions are referring to the Prosecution evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that non-Serb prisoners were murdered at detention facilities, at the police station, Territorial Defence building, Crkvina, and other locations in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that. I was not an eyewitness when any murder was committed or any mistreatment, and I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you cannot state whether or not you accept the evidence as to those facts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that non-Serb prisoners were forced to perform fellatio on each other at the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that prisoners, including Muhamed Bicic and Ibrahim Salkic, were brutally beaten at various detention facilities in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You do not accept that fact even though two of your co-defendants have pled to those charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that, and I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My answer is not whether you saw it, not whether you can confirm it. Do you accept it, especially after two of your co-defendants have admitted to such conduct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm saying that I did not see any of that and I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that Sulejman Tihic, the SDA president, was forced to go on Radio Samac and give a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that prisoners or labourers were forced to dig trenches with bullets flying past them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that prisoners and labourers were forced to loot homes of non-Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that and no evidence was presented here to support that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You did not hear the testimony of Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Esad Dagovic did not say whether that was a Serb house or a house that belonged to somebody else. Serb houses were looted during the war as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You did not hear the testimony of Nusret Hadzijusufovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that many non-Serbs were arrested on the basis of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only on the basis of ethnicity? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You do not accept any of those statements, sir. Let us continue. You were either the highest or a very high-ranking civilian in Samac in the civilian government in 1992 after April 17th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were a lowly official?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was never a member of the civilian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you president of the SDS municipal board in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you president of the Crisis Staff in Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: After April 17th. You know what the Crisis Staff was, sir. You've testified that you were president of it. Do you agree that you were president of the Crisis Staff in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that you were president of the War Presidency in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were president of the Assembly of the Samac Municipality, sir; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were representative to the Serbian Autonomous District of Semberija and Majevica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was nominated for that position, but I never attended and I never got a decision in writing stating that. I mean, from the Assembly of the SAO Semberija and Majevica, because when we adopted these documents, very soon after that this was abolished altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified on November 15th about document 101. It was -- and you state -- "this is a document that also speaks about the relations between the Serb Municipality of Samac and the SAO Semberija and Majevica. It was issued on that same date and it says you had certain representatives representing the Municipality of Bosanski Samac in SAO Semberija and Majevica. Is that right?" And you said "Yes." Do you recall that testimony and that answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps the accused should be shown document 101 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to refresh his memory. When you say "document 101," is it an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Exhibit P101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "And let me just add, sir, there is a correction from the interpreter. The representative of the Samac municipality in SAO Semberija and Majevica was in fact Dr. Simic himself." That's what the document says. Are you now denying you held that position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could I have the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me read this to you in English and they'll translate it to you. "The head of the Crisis Staff, Dr. Blagoje Simic. Shall represent the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac before the bodies and institutions of SAO Semberija and Majevica." Is that correct, what I just read? Is that what it says on that sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's just in -- when we are here with this document, it's -- in terms of the translation. Well, maybe it's the spirit of language, but in Article 1, in B/C/S language says "President of Crisis Staff, Simic Dr. Blagoje." And since we are operating here with these terms, it's very new -- new word here, "head of certain institution." Although I can confirm that probably it's the same thing. But for the clarity, I think we should -- we should proceed with the term of "president" or "vice-president" or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are wasting the Court's time. This is the last warning. You've had those documents as exhibits and you've had them. They were given to you. You never complained about any misleading translation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's not complaining --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Will you sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's okay. It's not complaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just sit down. The Prosecution may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No more need for that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Simic, do you agree that you held that position as representative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree that the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Samac proposed me to be a representative in the organs of the SAO Semberija and Majevica, but I do not agree that my nomination was accepted by the organs of the SAO Semberija and Majevica, because it's very far away geographically. It doesn't cover the municipality of Samac and I never got a decision in writing stating that I was accepted by that body. Our wish was one thing and possibilities were another.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that you held the position of deputy or vice-president of the Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia and you held that position until November -- I'm sorry, until November 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to refer to the annex to the joint statement of matters not in dispute. Page 12, "From 4 November 1991 through at least 30 November 1992, he," referring to Blagoje Simic, "was the deputy of the Assembly of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, with regard to the translation. What is the term "deputy"? Is it a deputy president or it is -- he's deputy as a member of certain institution of parliament? So we have to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The document --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or he's just a member of parliament.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The document was clear, and this is a document to which you had a part in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am referring to the -- to the translation, which we are receiving just right now. So maybe we could clarify that with the witness. Because there is two terms. Whether Dr. Simic was a deputy in terms of a member of certain institution, which is SAO or whatever, or he was a vice-president of the institution which title is SAO North Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall stick to the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll say it again: The annex to the joint statement of matters not in dispute state: "From 4 November 1991 through at least 30 November 1992, he" -- and we're referring to you "was the deputy of the Assembly of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, we're receiving a translation which is absolutely incorrect. Could -- my friend can clarify. What is his meaning of the "deputy of assembly"? Because the Translation Unit give us the translation that he was a vice-president of the Northern Bosnia. And are you referring that he was a deputy, in terms of -- in terms of member of parliament of SAO Bosnia? They are two different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This was an agreed document which contain this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. But the question is: Are we speaking now in the same terms and speaking about the language that -- in B/C/S language is coming to the ear of my client. That's my intervention. I'm not speaking about the fact that we made this agreement fact. So maybe he can explain in extended version, my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's the accused who should explain. He knows what portfolios he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, tell us what positions you held between the 4th of November, 1991, and the 30th of November, 1992 in that body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which body?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The Assembly of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a decision in writing with regard to any particular position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So now you claim that it is a matter in dispute. You no longer go along with your agreement that you were the deputy of the Assembly of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my testimony, I said that this SAO was not operating at all. Literally it did not exist at all. And I did not get a decision in writing --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is that you have stipulated that you were the deputy of that body. Are you now denouncing that stipulation? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you quote me where I admitted that. Where did I personally admit that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. I will read the whole paragraph of your stipulation. "Blagoje Simic, born 1 July 1960, is a medical physician from Kruskovo Polje, Bosanski Samac municipality. From 1991 to 1995 Blagoje Simic was president of the municipal chapter of the Serbian Democratic Party, SDS, in Bosanski Samac. Blagoje Simic was the vice-president -- I'm sorry, vice chairman of the municipal assembly from 1991 through 12 -- I'm sorry, through 17 April 1992. And from 4 November 1991 through at least 30 November 1992 he was the deputy of the Assembly of the self-declared Serb Autonomous Region of Northern Bosnia of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On or about 17 April 1992, Blagoje Simic was appointed president of the Crisis Staff in the Municipal Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosanski Samac and of the Municipality of Pelagicevo under formation. On or about 21 July 1992 the Crisis Staff was renamed the War Presidency of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac, and Blagoje Simic was named president of the War Presidency. On or about 22 January 1993 Blagoje Simic was elected speaker of the Samac Municipal Assembly and served in that position until 1996." That is your stipulation, sir. Are you now renouncing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is my signature there?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. But the name of your attorney is on the cover of it. Are you renouncing it, or is that still your stipulation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to the SAO Northern Bosnia, I renounce these stipulations because they are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you one of two representatives from Samac to the Assembly of Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean by "representative"? I was never an MP, a member of parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you a representative from your community of Samac to the Assembly of Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May we see Exhibit P124, please, and may that be shown to the defendant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to -- I invite your attention to page 13 of the gazette, decisions 1 and 2. I will read them. Decision 1: "The representatives of the Serbian people from the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation are hereby appointed." Decision 2: "Dr. Blagoje Simic and Mirko Dragisic are appointed representatives of the Serbian people from the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation in the Assembly of the Serbian People of BH," meaning Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we have certain problems to locate this particular decision, so could we have a reference of the top left number in the -- because there is a problem with the English original -- with the translation in English. So what is on the top left-hand corner, which number, so that we can follow -- we can locate this number in the Official Gazette number 1? Because page 13 -- we have only 12 pages. That's the problem with the original version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe we could go -- what is the ERN number of the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. You see, on that decision, you see on the left-hand -- just in the mid-way of the page, number 4. So that's the useful number that we need to have in order to find in Serbian language exact number, you know, because otherwise if you cannot make a reference with ERN number in B/C/S language, then we are lost. But now we can follow. So just follow the number on the left -- top left-hand side and we could resolve that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Maybe, Mr. Weiner, we can make sure that Mr. Simic is on the right page and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It doesn't say what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me read it again. "The representatives --" why don't you follow it along with me. "The representatives of the Serbian people from the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation are hereby appointed." Is that what it says in decision 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The word "representatives," yes. It says "predstavnici," yes, that's right. But not "zastupnici." And it doesn't say "narodni poslanici," either. In the sense of MPs, members of parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I said "representatives." I'm not asking you about members of parliament. I'm not asking you about anything else. My question is: Does it say those words that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me whether I was a zastupnik, a represent in that sense. I was not a zastupnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next sentence: "Blagoje Simic and Mirko Dragisic are appointed representatives of the Serbian people from the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation in the Assembly of the Serbian People of BH." Is that what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you move the document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representatives, predstavnici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. That's what it says, representatives. You were a representative --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representative as predstavnik, yes. And that basically doesn't mean a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for two different terms that my client is now trying to explain. There is one term in English language -- so when Dr. Simic makes reference to that issue, the same word is going on the display and in the earphones for these two terms, which according to his explanation are different. And maybe our friends from interpreter booths can clarify that. In fact, here we are speaking about a word in B/C/S is "zastupnici," which means that certain person is appointed by power of attorney and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the other word he's using --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, these are not in your documents which are coming on if scene now. You've had them as exhibits. You've read them. You've got instructions from your client. There is nothing new here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour. The problem is that my client right now makes in B/C/S, in his own native language, makes two different terms for one term in English, "representative." That's the basis of my objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are going to follow the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He is not, you know, a -- I don't know what's going on. I mean, it's not clear for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are going to follow the official translation. That's all. That's why we have official interpreters and translators in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, sir. Sir, you said you were a member of the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You stated that Miroslav Tadic was a member of the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You stated that Simo Zaric was not a member of the Crisis Staff. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But he was involved in various military and police matters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I heard that he was involved in police matters. Security issues within military service. That's another point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He was involved in various police, security, military matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And where did I describe what he dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's my question to you: Was he involved in various police, security, or military matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you don't know what involvement Simo Zaric had during April of 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't know what involvement Simo Zaric had in May of 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't know what, if any, involvement or activities Simo Zaric was involved in or performed in June of 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, or did I ever follow him or was I interested in what he was doing or were we friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that, sir. We're going to get to all of those topics. Let us continue. Sir, you indicated that -- you've testified that Stevan Todorovic was not a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you've testified that he has falsely stated that he was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Miroslav Tadic, a fellow member of the Crisis Staff, in Exhibit P138 has provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor and has stated at paragraphs 39 and 40 that Stevan Todorovic served on the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know any reason why Miroslav Tadic would lie about that or say that if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. Calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a perfect question. It's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any reason why Miroslav Tadic would say that if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any reason why Miroslav Tadic would state that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff if it wasn't true? Are you aware of any reason that Miroslav Tadic would state that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only if he had not been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the witness is being asked to speculate as to what another person thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's not speculation. This is cross-examination, and it followed upon the answer of the accused. It's a proper question, as far as the Trial Chamber is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry, Your Honour, is it time for the break now or are we going to break at 11.00 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We shall break now and continue our proceedings at 11.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we are still on the same topic, maybe it would be useful to have this portion of the interview of Mr. Tadic and maybe the accused can be familiarised with that. If there is certain references, because it's a long document, so maybe if my colleague would like to make certain references, then a certain portion could be read out to the defendant or show this particular part of the interview. That's the only suggestion of some proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When we left off, sir, we were talking about a member of the Crisis Staff stating that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff, was a fellow member of the Crisis Staff. And I'm going to read to you some paragraphs from his testimony. "Okay." This is a question from Nancy Paterson. Question, on page 39, which is -- which is Exhibit P138, Your Honour, the last question and answer. "Okay. I have to ask you a few more questions about the Crisis Staff. Can you tell us, you were members of the Crisis Staff besides you." It should be "who were members of the Crisis Staff besides you?" "Why not. As you know, the president of the Crisis Staff was Dr. Blagoje Simic. At first, to start with there was also Mirko Jovanovic, who I also did not know. At the multi-party elections, it was not the party elections in 1991 or whenever it was, I can't remember, but what it was, he became president of the executive board of the Municipality of Samac. He was from Orasje. I believe -- I presume because nobody knew him in Samac. And then there was Stevan Todorovic, Simeon Simic, Fadil Topcagic -- sorry, could you repeat whom I've already given names. Maybe I've forgotten someone." "Okay. It was Blagoje Simic, Mirko Jovanovic, Stevo Todorovic, Simeon Simic, Fadil Topcagic, you've told us before Milos Bogdanovic, yourself, so that's two, four, six, seven, counting yourself." Sir, I ask you again: Do you know any reason why Miroslav Tadic would say that Stevan Todorovic was a fellow member of the Crisis Staff if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Due to the fact that he hadn't been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let us continue. Are you aware that your co-defendant Simo Zaric in Exhibit P141 provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor and has acknowledged on page 7 that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff? Let me read that to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm reading from Exhibit 141, page 7, top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "Zaric: Well, the police commander was Stevan Todorovic and he was already a member of the Crisis Staff, which was newly formed." Sir, do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would say that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff if he wasn't a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any reason why would Simo Zaric know who the members of the Crisis Staff are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, sir. You haven't answered my question. Are you aware of any reason why Simo Zaric would make that statement if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. But I wish to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had no links to Simo Zaric, so I don't see how could he have known who the members of the Crisis Staff were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's the second time you've said that today, that you had no links to Simo Zaric. And you also said earlier that you were not aware of his actions or Simo Zaric's activities in June of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me what Simo Zaric had dealt with, and I told you that I didn't know about that. "Dealt with" means what kind of tasks he executed on a daily basis, was involved in, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that in June or late May or June of 1992 you went to Belgrade with Simo Zaric and others? Isn't that true, late May or June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that it is true that we met in Belgrade, and it is possible that we started out together, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was the trip for humanitarian reasons, sir? You went Miroslav Tadic, Simo Zaric, and Stevan Todorovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went with Miroslav Tadic, Milos Bogdanovic. And it just so happened that Stevan Todorovic was the driver, so he joined the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you let Stevan -- actually, first tell me: How far away from Bosanski Samac is Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over 200 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you let Stevan Todorovic, who you claim to be an alcoholic and abuser of pills, drive you that distance? Is that what you're trying to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you took him to this meeting of a humanitarian nature; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't take him anywhere. He crashed the party, so to speak. He joined on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you just let him join you and go all the way to Belgrade for humanitarian meetings or humanitarian meetings with Andjelko Maslic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't that I allowed him to come with us. He didn't ask for my consent. He didn't ask us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You went to a meeting with Andjelko Maslic and then you attended a 40-minute meeting at the Air Force command centre; correct? That's what you've testified to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were at the meeting with Andjelko Maslic, and then we went to have a coffee at Stevan Todorovic's best man's, because we had no other alternative.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was at the Air Force headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that that's right, but I'm not a hundred per cent sure. I don't think I would be able to find the place today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you told this Chamber that you don't recall what the discussion was during that 40-minute meeting; isn't that correct? Isn't that what you told this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I didn't remember the details, that we discussed all problems of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you travelled to Belgrade to have Crni approved at the new commander of the armed forces? Isn't that the real reason you went to that 40-minute meeting at the Air Force command centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was not the reason of our going there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you contacted Simo Zaric in the middle of the night and told him that he should join the delegation going to Belgrade? Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The meeting was organised by Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, didn't you also tell him in that telephone conversation that there was a task to be carried out, referring to Belgrade? Isn't that what you told him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's return to the exhibit from -- of the interview of Simo Zaric. And I want to read to you, on page 36, from Simo Zaric's statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. "I was called in the middle of the night by Mr. Blagoje Simic, who said to me that I should join this delegation going to Belgrade and that there was a task to be carried out. I asked what it was about, and he said that I should see once we were in Belgrade. I did not even think of refusing. Miroslav Tadic, that you know very well, was also asked the same thing. So the next day in the early morning we set off for Belgrade. Mr. Blagoje Simic, Mr. Stevan Todorovic, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, me, and then we were joined in Belgrade by Milos Bogdanovic, who was a member of the Crisis Staff and he was a Secretary for National Defence in Samac." Sir, do you know any reason why Simo Zaric would make that statement if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. This is a statement given by Simo Zaric, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would make that statement if it was not true or correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer the question that is put to me in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then let us continue, if you can't answer the question. Isn't it true the next day on the way to Belgrade you told Simo Zaric that you were going there to get Crni approved, referring to the new military commander's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. There is an intervention in the transcript. Page 45, line 3: The true and correct form of the answer of the defendant would be "I don't know how to answer to this question." It is not "I can't answer." I do not know how to answer on that question that is put to me in this form; that was the correct -- the correct answer of Dr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll accept that form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the next day on the way to Belgrade you told Simo Zaric that you needed to get to Belgrade to get Crni approved and you were referring to the position of new military commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say anything to Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's refer to page 36. "Already in the car we were told that all this was about Crni and we needed to get to Belgrade to get approval." Did you make that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm quoting from Simo Zaric's statement, page 36: "Already in the car we were told that all this was about Crni and that we needed to get to Belgrade to get approval." Is that your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you knew, sir, why you were going to Belgrade, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to Belgrade because of humanitarian problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's continue on that meeting that you don't recall at the Air Force command. Isn't it true at that meeting it was decided that Crni should be the military commander and that during this meeting you spoke with General Mladic on the phone, the alleged war criminal General Mladic? Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This information doesn't refresh your recollection to what happened at that meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me quote Simo Zaric, page 39 of his interview: "And after, Blagoje Simic spoke to General Mladic and he came back, he was all red and flushed. It was very easy to realise that he had been shouted at and Mladic had said to him apparently that he as president of the Crisis Staff had many civilian matters to attend and that he should not meddle in the appointments of brigade commanders. The general message was that he was far away and he wanted the matter settled and that this was not the way to do it but he just wanted the matter settled for once and for all." Do you recall -- do you recall that situation happening at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall speaking to General Mladic, sir, the war criminal, the alleged war criminal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would describe this type of meeting -- this wasn't a humanitarian meeting -- would describe that meeting in this way if it wasn't true or correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, by the way, did you ever meet with General Mladic in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came on one occasion to Samac after the arrest of Stevan Todorovic and Milan Simic, and that was the only time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
