utterances.text: Did you ever meet with General Mladic in the municipality or the town of Doboj in 1992 in October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With him personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll get back to that. Sir, let's talk about the paramilitaries or the strike battalion, as you described them, that arrived from Serbia. When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The defendant never said that the paramilitaries were the strike battalion. He said in the examination-in-chief that parts of the strike battalion were a certain number of volunteers. But with this kind of question, there is an equality between "paramilitaries" and the term of "strike battalion," so I ask to -- that this question should be correct. Because he never said that the volunteers are equal to strike battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll call them the volunteers, the assault group. If he'll answer a question, I'll call them whatever he would like, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's call them the volunteers. Sir, when did the volunteers arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you put a specific question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know when they arrived in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, when Crni and his group arrived? Do you know when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stories had it that it was on the 10th of April, 1992 -- the 10th or 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did you learn that they arrived on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think on the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you know how they arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In helicopters of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did they arrive, what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who sent them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P116, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you discuss the matter of the paramilitaries with an investigative judge in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's the statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed the original document, and this is a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at page 2, the second sentence of the second paragraph: "I know that Crni came to the Posavina for the first time on 10 April this year together with his assault group from Serbia, which arrived in helicopters and it landed in the village of Batkusa." Does that refresh your recollection of where the assault group arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me in which territory that group landed. You didn't ask me about a particular town or place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us, where did they arrive when they got to Bosanski Samac, to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Batkusa, municipality Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next sentence: "At that time the JNA still existed and they were sent by the Serbian MUP, Ministry of Interior, together with 18 of our own men who had been attending a training course in --" it's unclear what the word is -- "in Serbia." Is that correct, sir? Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is what correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What I've just read to you, is that what it says there? Would you like me to read it again? I'd be happy to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you asking me whether this is what is stated in this document or do you want me to confirm whether it is so? I did not read this paper. I signed it without reading it, and I do not accept that this statement was given under normal circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that very shortly, but what I first want to do is -- did I read that correctly? Let me read the next two sentences. Tell me if I read them correctly and then tell me if that's not what you said. "At that time --" I'm reading from the third sentence in the second paragraph -- or the first full paragraph, which indicates -- the first full paragraph. "At that time the JNA still existed and they were sent by Serbian MUP/Ministry of Interior together with 18 of our own men who had been attending a training course in --" can't be deciphered "in Serbia. It was those men that made up the assault battalion that carried out all the tasks assigned to it very successfully." Number one: Did I just read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you tell the investigating judge or prosecutor, did you tell or provide the investigating judge or prosecutor with that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not this way, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you deny that you made that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of statement I made because I did not read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you deny that you said that information to the investigating judge or prosecutor who took the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall now what I said then, but I talked about the conditions under which this was taken, and Stevan Todorovic did more of the talking more than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, this witness statement, right above that paragraph it says, "The witness stated the following." Is Stevan Todorovic's name on this witness statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Does this say "joint statement of Stevan Todorovic and Blagoje Simic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did Stevan Todorovic sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told the investigative judge that you were aware that 18 of your local residents had been attending a training course in Serbia and they helped make up the strike battalion with these volunteers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what I said to the investigative judge. After ten years, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you claim that you did this under stressful situations. Unlike the other witnesses in this case, were you under arrest when you provided a statement to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My health condition was very poor. People who were in authority were arrested. The clash between the military and the civilian government was evident in the ground and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop. That's not my question. My question to you was: Were you under arrest when you gave that statement? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I thought that I was under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified about this a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you never testified that you were under arrest at the time that you gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I described who was present and under what conditions. Since I was there, it looked as if I had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you previously testified that you were not under arrest at the time you gave this statement; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say now that I was under arrest either. I just said that it looked as if I was under arrest. It looked as if I was under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you were not under arrest at the time you provided that statement; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, unlike the other witnesses in this case, when you gave that statement you weren't in a beaten, bloodied, and bruised condition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My health condition was very serious because I had been wounded and I almost could not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the time when you shot yourself in the foot or the leg? Is that the wound you're talking about, almost six months earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You weren't in a bloodied condition at that time. You hadn't just been beaten. Isn't that correct, sir, when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Unlike the witnesses in this case, you weren't beaten during the statement; isn't that correct? You weren't beaten as part of the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Unlike the witnesses in this case, you weren't starving from a lack of food when you gave your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not compare myself to other witnesses in this case. At that time I was very undernourished.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat that answer. It doesn't make any sense, sir. You said you would not compare yourself to the other witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not compare myself to other witnesses in this case, but at that moment I was also very undernourished.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified about that statement previously, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On direct examination, on this statement. You testified on November 15th, 1992 [sic], do you recall testifying on direct examination and being questioned about that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's rather confusing for the witness. He said that Dr. Simic testified on November 15th, 1992. We heard that in our earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, November 15th, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We have a record here of 14 December, 1992. So we are little bit confused what he meant by this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You testified last week, November 15th, 2002 on direct examination or examination-in-chief about that statement; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you never said at that time that you were in pain while you gave the statement; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did I say now that I was in pain?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said you had pain because you shot yourself in the leg six months earlier, or you had trouble moving your leg. Are you now saying you were in pain when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you never said last week you were in pain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you never said last week that you were undernourished when you gave that statement; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was convalescing; that is to say, a patient who convalesces after a serious injury. I lost a lot of weight, a lot of kilogrammes and a lot of blood in that period. During the surgical operation the deep blood vessels were obliterated and the peripheral blood vessels were taking over the function of the deep blood vessels. The colour of my limb was changing and gangrene was constantly looming over me, and therefore my medical situation was so serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified about this last Friday, November 15th, 2002. You never stated that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I stated that the statement was taken under conditions that were not normal and under duress, that I did not have any legal counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is: You didn't make that statement about your medical condition last Friday when you were questioned by your attorney; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know where we are going with this kind of questioning. It wasn't even my question, so how a person can answer to a question which was never raised. So this is for the first time that he got this question. So don't make this confusion and make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, Mr. Pantelic, it's you who is wrong. I don't think you are understanding or following the questioning. There is nothing wrong with the questions that Mr. Weiner is putting to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking what was done in examination-in-chief, Your Honour. I never asked him about these issues; simply as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a very simple question: You never described having a medical problem at the interrogation when you testified last Friday, November 15th, 2002; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not correct. I tendered the history of my illness, the place where I was operated on. It says what the operation was like. It says there that I was a very serious patient and the human body cannot convalesce that quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is: When you described the circumstances surrounding the interrogation, you never stated that you were suffering from a medical problem. When you made that -- when you described that episode, you never said that last Friday; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But in the episode before that I explained that my health condition was poor for months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the episode before. I'm asking you about that specific episode. It's a very simple question. You never described any medical problems that you had during the interrogation when you testified last Friday, November 15th, 2002. It's a simple question. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not the question that was put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, answer it. Take that question, please. You never described any -- having any medical problems while you were being interrogated when you testified last week, last Friday, November 15th, 2002; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall every word I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You don't recall every word you said in this document either, so let's talk about it. This first paragraph about Crni arriving and 18 men -- 18 local men being trained and arriving with the paramilitaries, do you contest the validity of that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I contest the validity of that entire document, that is to say, from the first to the last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, is that your signature at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But before that, there is the sentence stating that it had not been read out to me. And my signature is on the original document, not on the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, does it state the following, the last two sentences before you signed: "I have nothing else to state. I do not wish to read the record since my statement was dictated out loud, so I signed the record without any comments." Is that what it says just above your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Legal people can mess things up in all sorts of ways. My request was to state it there that nothing was read out to me and that I would sign it only then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, there is a specific question. A part of the document you signed was read to you, and all counsel was asking whether that was stated on the document. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. My question, Dr. Simic, is: Who dictated the statement out loud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And you were there present and heard the dictation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I did not pay any attention to that. I had not had sufficient legal information. I was not aware of legal remedy. I did not have legal counsel. My health condition was very poor. There was pressure from all sides. I was not asked to come to testify as a witness, and I was never given the possibility to explain this. Nobody later called me in to explain this document, nor was I ever a witness at any trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified last week, not many days ago, on November 15th. You never stated that this whole statement is false or incorrect or wrong; isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have said that I do not accept it because it was taken under abnormal conditions. And when I say "do not accept," that is what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me read out -- let me read out the questions and answers that you made last week concerning how this was dictated and read.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell me, although of course you're not a legal expert. In these proceedings before a military court in other proceedings before the relevant courts, is a record compiled like here in the Tribunal where every word is recorded or does the person who is carrying out the examination, like the investigating judge, does that person then dictate what the person who was giving the answers said? Answer -- and I'm referring to page 12397 if the Court wants to follow along.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference is that when we had a normal conversation and then one of the prosecutors would make a summary, dictate this to the typist, and thus create this record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So he conveyed the content of your at the same time, not faithfully, word for word, but in abbreviated form, abridged form.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In abridged form. So you stated last week that this was your statement in abridged form. You're now stating today that this is not your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I described then also how the statement was taken. I did not read the document. It was not read out to me. I do not know what I signed. The conditions under which it was taken were abnormal. This was under duress. I did not have any legal counsel. I did not have any legal protection, and I was never called to testify about this document in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you never said last week that you were under duress when you gave your statement; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I gave it under abnormal conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you never said you were under duress last week when you gave the statement. Sir, last week you indicated two errors, and those referred to the next-to-last paragraph of -- the next-to-last paragraph of the statement and on the second page, the third paragraph. You never stated that any other section of this statement was incorrect; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which term I should use so that you would understand me. I really do not know how to use any legal terms. I'm using my own words. You cannot convince me now that something was normal when it was abnormal. The medical term for this was pathological. It was a pathological situation. It was an abnormal situation. One way or the other, regardless of whether you want to portray this way or that way, it was an abnormal, pathological situation. And in that situation, I cannot accept a document that was compiled then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question again is: Last week you testified that there were two errors in this statement. You did not say that this whole statement was incorrect or wrong or untruthful; isn't that right? Just answer the simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot give a simple answer. The Honourable Judges put questions to me during my testimony here, and I explained to Their Honours how abnormal the situation was, how I did not have legal counsel, how --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. I'm not asking you about the circumstances. I'm asking you about last week's testimony. You indicated that there were two errors in this statement. You never said that the whole statement was incorrect or wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you interested in the truth or are you interested in what you're trying to prove? Which words should I use to state that the situation was abnormal, pathological? I only know how to use medical terms, and I think that you understand me very well. As for this legal mess that you're trying to create, that's a different thing. I don't know how to answer that. I can only use my own words, and I know what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I think we've belaboured the point. It's clear that the accused will maintain what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, nowhere in this statement does it say when you talk about Crni that Crni led an assault battalion made up of rogues and criminals. You never said that. It's not included in this statement, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This statement that you gave to the military. In no place did you state -- or is it indicated in this statement that Crni was leading a group of rogues and criminals; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I do not accept this statement, that I do not know what I had signed, and that I cannot give answers to things that are stated in that document. I cannot give reliable answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you tell that investigative judge that Crni led a group of rogues and criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten years later I do not know what I said to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You didn't state to the investigative judge or prosecutor that Lugar, who was discussed in this statement, was a mass murderer and killed 16 civilians, non-Serb civilians, in Crkvina. You didn't state that, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what I stated. There is the possibility that I did state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: However, nowhere within this statement that you signed does it have -- does it have that notation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have not shown me the original document yet. What you have there is a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, what we have in evidence is P116, and that's what we can show you. My question to you again is: Is there any indication in that statement about the crimes that Lugar committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, could you please look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is mentioned here is Crni only, if I read this right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, three paragraphs from the bottom, on page 3 it talks about the corridor being closed. Were you aware that the Posavina Corridor was closed after the kidnapping of Milan Simic and Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time when they were arrested, the corridor was closed, but I think that there were a number of reasons for that and that later came out during the trial in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that Crni and his battalion shut down the corridor with the support of the Samac War Presidency given subsequent to the closing of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The War Presidency did not pass any decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they make a verbal authorisation or statement supporting the closing of the corridor, as it says here in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what is in the statement of a military prosecutor who is conducting an interview with a representative of a civilian authority at the time when there was a major polarisation between these two segments of the society.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But sir, you're not just a representative of a civilian authority. You're an educated man. You're a medical doctor. You're a highly educated -- you might have been far more educated than the person who interviewed you, and you signed this document as your statement; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How did you come up with the conclusion that a doctor is more educated than a lawyer or a judge, or how can you conclude that a physician can know more about law than they do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Dr. Simic, you are not there to ask counsel questions. You are there to answer questions. So just answer the questions. If you don't know, you say so. If you haven't understood the question, you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you as a doctor and educated man signed that document as your statement? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I say is true. And I would ask the interpreters to address me in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Dr. Simic, I'm a little unclear why you're asking the interpreters to address you in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they're putting in Croatian words and then I repeat them here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. You would like separate the Croats from the Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's just that these two languages are separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's move on. Speaking of the paramilitaries, you indicated that you were aware, at least by the 15th, that they had arrived and were in the municipality of Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were aware that the -- I won't use "paramilitaries." -- the volunteers and strike battalion had arrived and were in the municipality of Bosanski Samac on or about April 15th -- or they arrived on the 10th and you became aware on the 15th. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer to that question is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just testified maybe 30 minutes ago that you became aware that the paramilitaries had arrived on or about the 15th of April. That's when you just said you became aware that they arrived. Are you now giving us a new answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thirty minutes ago I asked you to be more precise. I have never used the term "paramilitary formation." Second, you said when -- you asked when Crni came with his group. You never linked up the strike battalion with Crni. And now you're asking me about Crni and the strike battalion. There was no strike battalion during those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, the strike -- the assault group is the term you used. Crni and his group of volunteers, you realised or learned that they had arrived on or about the 15th of April, basically a day before the war; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And on or about the 15th or 16th of April, did you have some conversation with Crni or with Colonel Nikolic concerning war activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you involved through Colonel Nikolic in the takeover of Bosanski Samac, the military takeover of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you contact Colonel Nikolic on or about the 16th of April, 1992 and tell him that the Crisis Staff has decided to take over the town of Samac? Did you make that telephone call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no Crisis Staff at the time, and I didn't say that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go to Exhibit 141, the statement of Simo Zaric which was made to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 2nd of April, 1998. Question, on page 7: "Did you ever find out whether Blagoje Simic played any role in giving the orders for the attack to take place?" Answer by Simo Zaric: "I already told you that Nikolic told us that it was President Blagoje Simic, president of the Crisis Staff, had called him and told him that the Crisis Staff had decided that they would take over the town. So yes, I do believe that he played a key role in the takeover." Sir, do you recall making that telephone call to Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Simo Zaric made that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would give that statement if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's go on. Simo Zaric further states, the question: "When was it that Nikolic received this call from Simic informing him that they made the decision to take over?" Answer: "And Nikolic told us that he had received the call from Blagoje Simic on the 16th after midnight. So it was actually the 17th, very, very early in the morning -- in the night telling him that the Crisis Staff had decided to take over the town of Samac and that it would become the Serbian Municipality of Samac, that there were Serbian police and units were taking over all the vital buildings and objects of the town." Sir, were you aware that Simo Zaric has made that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And again, do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would make that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor if it was not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know of any bias or prejudice that would make Simo Zaric say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move to Exhibit P25, please. Sir, in June of 1992, by that time you were aware of the massacre of non-Serb civilians at Crkvina by Lugar and others; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are putting a question to me in such a way that it's very difficult for me to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had information that something like that had occurred, and as to whether it indeed had occurred will be established by the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he's making any reference to P25, it would be fair for the witness -- for the defendant to have this exhibit in front of him so that he can make certain comments. Simply as that. Because he made a reference to P25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then if you're speaking about a certain exhibit, the defendant is entitled to have it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was going to get to it a little bit later, but fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem if it is later --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Show it to him --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to keep this relation. When you are speaking about certain topics which are included in certain exhibit, it's perfectly clear that the defendant should have that in front of him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, and you've also testified last week about the problems that were caused by Crni and his volunteers from Serbia, the daily problems caused by them. You testified about that too, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to be as precise as possible in my answers, but I also want precise questions. Where did I mention Crni? I spoke about Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You talked about the volunteers and the trouble caused by the volunteers. Didn't you talk about that or testify about that last week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then I singled out Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. But you had talked about Lugar and the others; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then I singled out Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you knew Aleksandar Vukovic, nicknamed Vuk, was a member of the volunteers and was killed in action; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally, but I know that he had been killed in Samac as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he -- and his body was sent back by helicopter to Serbia, where he had come from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came from Montenegro, and his body was sent back to Montenegro. He's a Montenegrin by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it was sent back through Serbia when they removed certain prisoners and let them off in Serbia. But let's move on. This volunteer, Vuk, were you aware that this man in April -- in April or May of 1992 had attacked Simo Zaric while in the offices of the Crisis Staff? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to intervene at this point. Obviously the information that the Prosecutor is referring to is the cross-examination of Stevan Todorovic that I performed. And I never said that this incident happened in the Crisis Staff premises. It happened actually in the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to, Your Honour, the testimony of Simo Zaric before the OTP, before the Office of the Prosecutor when he gave his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When he was interviewed by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 141 at page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is, regardless of the place, it wasn't Bosanski Samac. And were you aware that this Vuk shoved his gun or pistol into Simo Zaric's mouth? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you were aware, sir, or you had at least heard that the volunteers, Lugar and other volunteers, had murdered a group of non-Serbs, 16 non-Serbs in Crkvina. You had received that information; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received information that this had happened. And as to whether it indeed had happened, that is something for the Court to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So after this incident happens where Lugar and other volunteers -- if you want to use your language -- allegedly commits a mass murder, what do you do? You establish the Aleksandar Vukovic Vuk Foundation, named after one of the volunteers. Isn't that true? Isn't that what you did in P25?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking too many questions. Please put a single question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you established the Aleksandar Vukovic Vuk Foundation on June 27th, 1992. That's what the Crisis Staff did in this document and you signed it. A foundation named after one of the volunteers, the same group of volunteers that committed a mass murder in your community. Did you establish that foundation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you use the term "you," what do you have in mind? I personally did not establish anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac establish the Vuk -- Aleksandar Vukovic Vuk Foundation at its session of 27 June 1992 and that in this document, Exhibit P25, you signed that and made it official?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we continue on?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Exhibit P75, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, rather than repeat what we've just discussed, to do it briefly, again you sent this letter on -- the date is illegible. So it's either the 12th or the 22nd of May, because there's some sort of slash in front of the "2." But I'll even say the 2nd of May. I'll give you the benefit of the doubt. You sent this letter to the Serbian people of Vranja; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This letter was sent by the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac to the Municipality of Vranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you stated in that letter that he was now -- that he is now a hero of the Serbian people from this area. Do you consider Crni and his volunteers heroes -- either Crni or his volunteers or both to be heroes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not a compact group. Crni was the only one who was from Vranja, and all the others were from Kragujevac. There was an antagonism between them the entire time. Crni was a citizen or resident of Samac. He married a woman from Samac and established his family there. The purpose of this letter was not any of these things mentioned, but there was another reason, because they wanted to establish economic cooperation between the factories producing furniture and textile. There were leading factories in Serbia, and we tried to establish economic cooperation. Nobody replied to this letter of ours from Serbia. We tried basically to start up the manufacturing process.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you state that Crni was a hero of the people -- of the Serbian people from this area? Is that what you stated in your letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not my letter. This is a letter sent by the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Didn't you sign that letter, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed all of the documents of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac that were brought to me, and this fell within the scope of my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you -- did the letter you sign state that Crni was a hero of the Serbian people from this area? Does your letter state that? The first paragraph, sir. Why don't I do this: Why don't I read it and you just tell me if I'm reading it correctly. The last -- it says -- in the last two sentences it appears to be of the first paragraph. And it's an abbreviated next-to-last sentence. "He is now a hero of the Serbian people from this area. The Serbian people from this area wish to thank the people of Vranja officially for raising such a son." Did I just read your letter correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But it says here "a favourite," not a "hero."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So he is a favourite of the Serbian people from the area of Bosanski Samac. And this is Crni, the volunteer from Serbia we're talking about. Could you read that section that I just read for the record so we can -- there might be a problem in translation. I don't want there to be any problem here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "And now a favourite of Serb people from our area, Dragan Djordjevic, Vranjanac, our Serb people wish to express officially their gratitude to the people of Vranja for raising such a son."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions on that document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like me to take the break now or continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, a while ago, when we started this, at about 9.45, we talked about the Serb Autonomous District of the Northern Bosnia Assembly. And you indicated that the assembly never really got going and that you were nominated but you were never given this -- given any position. We have obtained the minutes from a meeting which you attended of the Serbian Autonomous District and would like to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We have copies. We have it in English and B/C/S for the witness, or whoever needs it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not so sure, Your Honour, but I think that the Prosecution already tendered this document as an exhibit. I believe during the examination-in-chief of Mr. Sulejman Tihic it was done or something. So -- because it's very -- very hard to read this -- the small letters on this copy. If you have it in your...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall take a break and the parties can deal with that. The break will be about 20 minutes. We'll resume sitting at 12.50 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Instead of the document that we gave, can we go to Exhibit P10. Apparently the document that we just handed in has a different ERN number, but that and P10 are the exact same documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So this one which you handed in, we ignore it completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just ignore it, because other than the ERN number, it's the exact same as P10. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll deal with P10.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at Exhibit P10, please. Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I would like to read under the heading, "Excerpts from the minutes." And just tell me if this is correct. It says, "Excerpts of the minutes of the founding session of the Serb Autonomous District, Northern Bosnia Assembly, held on 4/11/1991 at 1600 hours in Doboj." Is that correct, what I just read, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what it says here in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue to the - one two, three - the fourth paragraph. "According to the conclusions of the board preparing the founding of the assembly, the following persons were nominated and elected to the chair: Dr. Blagoje Simic, Milovan Bjelosevic, Miljana Sajinovic, Miladin Nedic, and Nikola Perisic." Is that correct, what I just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bjelosevic Milovan. Bjelosevic Milovan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that correct what I just read? Those persons were nominated and elected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were nominated and elected to the chair.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page. AD-2B: "Dr. Blagoje Simic presented to the representatives the proposition for establishing of the Assembly of the Serb Autonomous District Northern Bosnia. After his presentation, the representatives voted by unanimous vote in favour of the decision to establish the Assembly of the Serb Autonomous District Northern Bosnia and confirm Doboj at its seat." Is that correct, what I just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you go to the last page, because there was -- you weren't certain about an election or any position that is you held, so I'd like to invite your attention to the last page, the second paragraph, last sentence: "Milovan Bjelosevic, professor, was elected vice-president with 17 votes in favour, and Dr. Blagoje Simic was elected vice-president with three votes in favour." Did I just read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were elected the vice-president, one of the two of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody asked me whether I would accept to be vice-president on the basis of three votes. First of all, I did not even obtain a democratic majority there. Secondly, nobody ever sent a decision in writing to me. Thirdly, my municipality did not delegate me there, because the municipality of Samac was not in the SAO of Northern Bosnia, nor did it ever declare its views on that. I never again attended these meetings, and as far as I know this SAO was not operating either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you attend that founding meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And according to the minutes, you were elected vice-president.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation needs to be explained. I was then doing my residency in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm not asking you about all the circumstances in your life. The question is: You were elected vice-president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of democratic procedure, this is impossible. It is impossible. 51 persons were voting, and then one obtains three votes and then gets elected? That's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you for legal opinion. Does it say here that you were elected vice-president? In fact, prior to that -- let's even step back. If we look at AD-2E: "As proposed by Savo Knezevic, chairman of the elections and appointments committee, the following persons were nominated for the positions of president and two vice-presidents of the assembly: Milovan Bjelosevic from Derventa, Nikola Perisic from Teslic, and Dr. Blagoje Simic from Bosanski Samac." Did I just read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then below that it says: "The results of the secret vote for president and two vice-presidents of the assembly were established as follows: Nikola Perisic, lawyer, was elected to the position of president of the assembly with 32 votes in favour; Milovan Bjelosevic, professor, was elected vice-president with 17 votes in favour; and Dr. Blagoje Simic elected vice-president with three votes in favour." Isn't that what the document says, you were elected vice-president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what is written on this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were in fact elected vice-president, or do you deny that? You can deny it if you'd like. Were you elected or weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, no. If I understood what "in fact" means.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, I -- well, could you please show me where it says that you were not elected vice-president or that you refused the position. Could you please show me that, where it says that on this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know whether this is an authentic document. I haven't confirmed it as such. Secondly, this is minutes -- or rather, an excerpt from minutes. So it's not even the complete minutes. Thirdly, no one ever gave me a decision in writing, because even if somebody is elected to a particular position at a meeting, then the legal staff have to write a decision thereon. Nobody ever issued that kind of decision in writing to me. Fourthly, my municipality did not declare itself in favour of acceding to this SAO. I could not attend any following meetings because I did not have support for that. And fifth, as far as I know, this SAO never again met; not even during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that this document is wrong and you were not elected vice-president, as it indicates in Exhibit 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I say that I was not elected vice-president because I did not get a decision in writing. And on the basis of three votes, that is impossible anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 71, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Weiner, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you have a chance to look at the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This document was discussed, document P71 -- or Exhibit P71 on Thursday, November 14th, last week when we were here. And you indicated that the signature on that was not yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the Crisis Staff enacting this order or decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the Crisis Staff did not pass this kind of decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of an order by the Crisis Staff to isolate Croatian civilians in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of an order by another municipal body to isolate Croatian civilians in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Croatian civilians were being isolated, arrested, detained, set aside in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had information from Stevan Todorovic that one day a certain number of civilians were brought to the cultural centre in Crkvina and that then on the same day they were returned to their homes with an apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of a longer term isolation of Croatian civilians in May and June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the way this information was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Other than that incident with Todorovic, other than that Crkvina incident, were you aware of large numbers of civilians who were arrested, detained, brought to various locations, including Zasavica, the high school gymnasium, were you aware of that happening in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for Zasavica, I don't know that anybody was ever arrested or that there was any kind of prison there. Stevan Todorovic reported to the Crisis Staff that there were some prisoners, and he claimed that there was enough evidence for criminal charges to be brought against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is an isolation of Croatian citizens, and my question was: Other than that incident with Todorovic, other than the Crkvina, other than the Crkvina incident, were you aware of a large number of civilians who were arrested, detained, brought to various locations, including Zasavica and the high school gymnasium, were you aware of that happening in May of 1992, a large-scale number of people, Croatians, being isolated, being detained -- arrested and detained in facilities or prisons, large numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What does this word "large numbers" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's even reduce the large number. Were you aware of a plan to isolate Croatian citizens, Croatian civilians in May of 1992, or that it was happening? Croatian civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew what Stevan Todorovic told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. Just for the sake of clarity, twice you've asked the question -- you talk about isolation centres, detention centres, and so on. And then you say, "Such as Zasavica, the high school gymnasium." Now, I'm sure we all take it that you mean the high school gymnasium in Bosanski Samac, but it reads as though it's the high school gymnasium attached to the village of Zasavica at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that a plan was made and implemented to isolate -- use the word "isolate" or "isolation" -- to isolate Croatian citizens, where they were arrested and detained at the high school gymnasium in Bosanski Samac and Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any plan to isolate Croatian citizens in May or June, arresting or detaining them because they were Croatian, and isolating them -- I'm using the words "isolate" or "isolation" of Croatian citizens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a very complex question. Stevan Todorovic reported that he did have prisoners for whom he was collecting documents and he was convinced that a criminal complaint could be filed against them and that these persons could be brought to trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What I'm talking about are not the prisoners at the SUP. I'm talking about prisoners who were isolated, civilians, that they isolated them mainly in response to the Serbs being held in Odzak. In response to the Serbs being held in Odzak, authorities went out, rounded up or arrested numbers of Croatian civilians and isolated them. Were you aware of that happening in May and June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipality of Samac during the first days of the war included almost only Serb territory. In its territory there was not a single Croat village almost. The Croats remained in their part of the territory, and they had their own municipality, Bosanski Samac Domaljevac. In the areas of Domaljevac, Bazik Grebnica, Prud, and at that time they also had Zasavica and Tisina under their control. Then the army managed to rectify part of the front line. I'm primarily referring Zasavica and Tisina, and the population withdrew before the army. So in the territory of the municipality and from the Croat villages, information was coming in that there was no one, that there was no one there, that the Croat population stayed within their own municipality or they withdrew before the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Weiner, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll take your answer as no, that you were not aware. Sir, Bosanski Samac is not a large municipality. It's not a metropolis. It's not New York city. It's not Tokyo. We're not talking about millions of people or a very, very large area. Do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of that is relative. But I can agree that it's a small municipality and a small town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if a large number of non-Serbs, a large number of the non-Serb population were suddenly rounded up, detained and isolated, you in this relatively small municipality, as you refer to it, would know about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that you are nevertheless trying to prove your own thesis. I said that a small number of civilians were in Crkvina and released on the same day. I said that Zasavica was never a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not my question and I'm not referring to Crkvina. My question to you was: So if a large number of non-Serbs, a large number of the non-Serb population were suddenly rounded up, detained and isolated, you in this relatively small municipality, as you refer to it, would know about it, wouldn't you? Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is too general a question. I don't know how to answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing -- there's nothing wrong with the question. It's perfectly clear. You were a resident of that place, so you should answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll ask it again. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He didn't say he didn't understand the question, so he should answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question is: So if a large number of non-Serbs, a large number of the non-Serb population were suddenly rounded up, detained and isolated, you in this relatively small municipality, as you refer to it, would know about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you define "a large number" for me. What is a large number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Over 100.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P82, please. Your Honour, could we go into closed session for a few moments, as we discuss this one document. It concerns a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 40 of Exhibit 141, Nancy Paterson questioning Simo Zaric on April 2nd, 1998. "My question wasn't whether you went to Zasavica and you were there for the exchange. My question is: What do you know about all these people from Samac that were collected, taken from their homes, and detained in the village of Zasavica?" Zaric: "It is a Croatian village and a number, as far as I know, of inhabitants remained after the outbreak of conflict. Before the conflict, some left, presumably to go to Croatia or to other villages in the area. The Samac Crisis Staff had decided at some point - I know that -" sorry. "The Samac Crisis Staff had decided at some point, I know that, I don't know when the decision was made, on the isolation of Croats and they were then -- a number of them were taken from Samac and put in these -- placed in these abandoned houses in Zasavica or made to -- for them accommodation to be provided by those people already living there. I don't think it was a camp in a typical sense because they were able to walk about, but certainly I know about the decision and this one was very unfortunate, a very bad decision by the Crisis Staff." Continuing, so this was the Crisis Staff -- this is question. "So this was the Crisis Staff in Samac at some point decided that the Croats living in Samac municipality should be removed from their homes and sent to Zasavica." It continues on to page 41, Your Honour, same exhibit. Zaric: "This was not exclusively for Croats because there were also some Muslim families there, I believe. The decision was made following the imprisonment of those people in the Odzak area. I think it wasn't just for Croats." Nancy Paterson: "But the people were forced to leave their homes and to go to Zasavica; is that right?" Zaric: "Yes." Nancy Paterson: "And what happened that these homes and the property they left behind?" Zaric: "Yes. This is what happened. And at first what happened is that the authorities of Samac had put in these houses and flats some of their new key people that they had from elsewhere. Later on Serbs from Krajina and refugees from elsewhere were placed into these houses. As far as their property is concerned, it had the same fate as the property of many others I've mentioned before, is that the paramilitaries and all those criminals thoroughly looted many houses and flats in Samac and many, many goods were taken away." That's how Simo Zaric describes the isolation decision by the Samac municipality, the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality. Do you have any reason or do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would not have told the truth at this time or would have told something other than the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any bias or prejudice that Simo Zaric would have which would make him answer in this manner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's continue. Page 43, still on Exhibit 141. Nancy Paterson: "Okay. How was it then that you know that the Crisis Staff is the one who made this decision to isolate these people in Zasavica?" Simo Zaric answers: "It was no secret. It was a well-known fact. Everything that was decided was well known. For instance, that the people were going to be taken to Crkvina and that they were detained in two schools, it was all well known. There was no secret about it."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That shows that. That confirms that, because there were never civilians at school in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric indicated that it was a well-known fact that the Crisis Staff decided to isolate people and that everything else that was done, placing people in Crkvina, detaining them in schools, that was also well known. Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would have made that statement if it wasn't true, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any bias, prejudice on Mr. Zaric's part which would make him state -- make a statement that was not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue on, since we're talking about detention and arrests and we're talking about Simo Zaric. Did you have a conversation with Simo Zaric on approximately April 26th to 28th, 1992 concerning the movement of prisoners to Brcko? It could have been a day or two later. About April 26th to 28th, 1992 concerning the movement of prisoners to Brcko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you and Stevan Todorovic confront Simo Zaric over his involvement in having prisoners transferred from the TO to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware again that Simo Zaric gave a statement on April 2nd, 1998 concerning this conversation between you and Todorovic and him in relation to the transfer of prisoners from the TO to Brcko? Are you aware that a statement was made by Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't read his statement in detail because I have an opinion of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in your opinion. I'm asking whether or not you had this conversation on or about April 26th to 28th, 1992 with Simo Zaric. That's all I'm asking, not your opinion on whether or not prisoners should be -- no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to read this to you and see if you recall this situation. Page 23, Exhibit 141, Nancy Paterson: "How was it that Todorovic and Simic, who apparently were in charge of arresting these people, how was it that they allowed you to remove these people?" Answer by Simo Zaric: "They did not know that night that this action would be carried out, but the next day I already had big problems because of this. They told me the army had nothing to do with these people, that they were not at all in our area of authority. They had asked me why I had done it. I said that it was all coordinated with the command -- with the security command of the higher command and this is how I got out of it, by saying that I was just doing what they had instructed." Having heard Simo Zaric's statement -- statement concerning this conversation, does that refresh your recollection as to the occurrence of this conversation with you and Stevan Todorovic and Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not participate in that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know any reason why Simo Zaric would have described this conversation with you and Stevan Todorovic if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any bias or prejudice on behalf of Simo Zaric which would make him provide a statement concerning a conversation between himself and you and Stevan Todorovic if it was not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to move on to another disagreement involving you and Stevan Todorovic on one side and Simo Zaric on the other. It occurred approximately April 19th or 20th at the Crisis Staff offices, and it occurred -- and it concerned who was in charge as well as the use of the radio station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 1992, yes, Your Honour. April 19th/20th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It concerned who was in charge, who was in power, as well as the use of the radio station. Do you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the time when the Crisis Staff did not have its premises. On the 19th of April, 1992 the Crisis Staff did not have its premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall your testimony that for a few days you were using the Agropromet or agricultural building? Do you recall that testimony, that you used that for a few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To have a meeting, yes, but those were not premises of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, at your meeting place, do you recall a conversation between -- involving you and Stevan Todorovic on one side -- you and Stevan, you and Todorovic, and Simo Zaric on the other side where there was a disagreement as to who was in charge of Bosanski Samac as well as the use of the radio station? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What's unusual, sir, is last week you indicated that the radio station wasn't functioning; however, what I'm going to discuss is a debate relating to the use of the radio station, the same one that you said wasn't functioning. Do you recall telling Simo Zaric on that occasion that you and Todorovic were in power?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that conversation, and I continue to claim that the radio station did not work at the time for two reasons: First, there was no power; and second, the transmitter had burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling Simo Zaric - let's take the first part - that you and Todorovic were in charge, were in power? And that's on page 15 of Exhibit 141.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never used such words. It is absolutely not my style. I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you make this statement: "While with Todorovic and Simic, they told me that I was no longer any factor of power, that they were in power. I was nothing, and that my job was to look after the borders and I not should be meddling in the affairs of the town." Do you recall that conversation involving you and Stevan Todorovic on one side and Simo Zaric on the other side? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the second part of the conversation, that Simo Zaric should not have put out a radio announcement on the 4th Detachment? And there was further discussion concerning the use of the radio station. Do you recall any of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me read page 15 of Exhibit 141. "They also said to me, why did you put that announcement of the 4th Detachment in the radio? By that time what was going out on the radio was their press staff announcement about the creation of the Serbian Municipality of Samac. Also, what they did later on was to bring -- then I learned they were bringing Sulejman Tihic, the president of the SDA, who had gone on radio to say that the Muslims should accept the creation of the Serbian municipality, and I believe that this supposed speech of Mr. Tihic had been written and directed by Todorovic and Simic." Sir, does that refresh your recollection as to the conversation that occurred at your Crisis Staff meeting office between you and Stevan on one side and Simo Zaric on the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This did not take place at the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you want to break now or should I ask a few more questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we can continue on questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, based on the discussion that I've just read to you, which Simo Zaric says was between him and you and Todorovic, would you like -- would you now like to change your testimony that the radio station was in fact functioning and Sulejman Tihic was broadcasting, Simo Zaric was broadcasting about the 4th Detachment, that the municipality was broadcasting about the new Serbian Municipality of Serbian Samac? Would you now like to change your testimony that the radio station was functioning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I say that there was no electrical power, that the transmitter had burned down, that the Municipal Assembly had to procure one in the following month, that we bought a wrong one for mid-waves and that nobody had radios that could receive that and that nothing functioned as it should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you my last two question, as I have in the past: Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would make that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor if the statement was not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of any bias or prejudice which would force Simo Zaric or would induce Simo Zaric to make that -- to make a false statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn and continue tomorrow at 9.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
